items.title: The algebraic curvature step in Bakry–Émery interpolation

source.edition: Chewi, An Introduction to Sampling, edition 2026-08-09
source.attribution: Sinho Chewi defines Γ₂ and CD(α,∞); Samplinglib records their immediate pointwise algebraic consequence.

items.statement: For a linear generator satisfying CD(α,∞), the expression LΓ(f)−2Γ(f,Lf) is pointwise at least 2αΓ(f).
assumptions: An arbitrary state type and a real-linear generator on real-valued observables.
A certificate of CD(α,∞), including α>0 and the pointwise inequality αΓ(f)≤Γ₂(f).
An arbitrary observable f and state x.

obligations.label: Expand Γ₂ and derive the exact lower bound used in backward interpolation

bindings.boundary: No semigroup construction, derivative identity, order preservation, analytic domain closure, or concrete diffusion curvature verification is asserted.

assumption_deltas.source: Chewi Definitions 1.2.28–1.2.29 state Γ₂ and CD(α,∞).
assumption_deltas.lean: Samplinglib writes α>0, every function/point quantifier, the one-half normalization, and both mixed terms directly in the audited theorem signature.
assumption_deltas.reason: The conclusion is the exact algebraic consequence obtained by specializing the fully expanded curvature inequality and multiplying it by two.
